title: DR1 lets a user start any task on the hub from the first visit; the frontend greys nine of its eleven rows out as "Cannot start yet" until a country of origin and a commodity have been answered.

finding.frontend: On a notification where only the country of origin has been given, nine of the eleven hub rows carry no link and read "Cannot start yet" — Main reason for importing, Additional commodity details, Animal identification details, Arrival details, Transporter, Roles and addresses, Contact address, Uploaded documents and Check and submit. Only "Where is this consignment coming from?" and "What are you importing?" can be opened. The whole task list is held behind two answers: the country of origin and a commodity selection, the two obligations enforced at continue in src/server/app/bridge/obligation-source.js:31-34. A row is offered only when the first page behind it clears that check (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:103-123); otherwise the row is rendered without a link and its real status is replaced by "Cannot start yet" (:95).
finding.prototype: Every row of DR1's task list is a link on every visit, whatever has been answered. The hub view model gives each of the twelve items a fixed href and one of exactly two statuses, "To do" or "Complete" (app/routes.js:5749-5841), so a user who has just created a notification can go straight to Transport details or Upload documents if that is what they have to hand.
finding.difference: Stop withholding hub rows. Render every task row as a link and let its status describe progress instead of permission, which means dropping the gate consulted in controller.js:120 and the "Cannot start yet" substitution at :95, and letting each page cope with being opened before its neighbours. The frontend's "cannot start" state is not the same thing as a page being unreachable: the questions behind the blocked rows are still asked, because a new notification is walked forward through origin, commodity search, commodity details, reason for import, animal identification and additional details before it ever lands on the hub (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39), and once a commodity exists every answer row unblocks — the fe-hub capture, taken one answer later, shows ten of the eleven rows startable, the exception being Check and submit, which stays shut until the rest are done and is its own finding. What DR1 gives and the frontend does not is the choice of where to start.
finding.falsifiedBy: A frontend hub rendered with neither a country of origin nor a commodity answered in which the Arrival details or Uploaded documents row is a working link.
finding.verification: Opened the fe-hub-no-commodity, fe-hub and dr1-notification-hub DOMs and all three screenshots, and read bridge/obligation-source.js:29-34, flow/prerequisites.js, flow/gates.js:16-32, flow/navigation.js:20-25, hub/controller.js:93-123, linear/flow/run.js:22-53, flow/run-state.js, shared/kit.js:92-101 and dashboard/controller.js:117, plus routes.js:5749-5841. Ran the falsifier against fe-hub-no-commodity and counted from the markup: exactly nine <li> elements carry `govuk-task-list__status--cannot-start-yet` and no <a>, and they are the nine the finding names; the two open rows are origin and commodities. Followed the journey rather than the task list, since a dead row is evidence about the row: `ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE` is countryOfOrigin and commoditySelection, `pagePrerequisites` turns those into a prerequisite for every later flow page, and `rowGatePasses` consults only `row.pages[0]` — so the block really is those two answers. The forward path holds: `beginOpeningRun` fires when the dashboard creates a notification, RUN_STEPS walks origin, commodity search, commodity details, reason for import, purpose, animal identification, additional details and only then returns the hub path, and `pageRoutes` attaches no gate to any of those routes, so the blocked rows describe a state the user passes through rather than a wall. DR1's twelve items — three, three, three, one, one, one across the six sections, the identification and transit rows being conditional — each carry a literal href and one of the two statuses, confirming the always-a-link claim from source as well as from the ten links in the capture. RUBRIC 2 FIRED on one clause: the difference slot said the fe-hub capture "shows all eleven rows startable". It does not — Check and submit reads "Cannot start yet" in that capture too, so it is ten of eleven, and the eleventh is blocked by the review gate rather than by the origin-and-commodity gate this finding is about. Corrected in place. Everything else stands.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: "every row unblocks the moment a commodity exists — the fe-hub capture, taken one answer later, shows all eleven rows startable". TRUE: ten of the eleven. In the fe-hub capture the Check and submit row is still a bare <li> reading "Cannot start yet", because it is held by the review section's own gate (`scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers`) rather than by the page prerequisites this finding describes. CHECKED against the fe-hub DOM and screenshot and against hub/controller.js:81-83 and flow/section-status.js:11-15. The nine-of-eleven claim about fe-hub-no-commodity, which is what the title rests on, is unaffected.

relatedTo.why: the Check and submit row is blocked by the same mechanism, but its replacement of DR1's always-available Review and submit button is a separate change
the same gate, but that row never unblocks at all, so removing the gate fixes both
